source_text: Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ γεγονότες οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ λελατρεύκασι τῇ κτίσει, καὶ θεὸν ἐκάλουν τὸν οὐρανὸν, χρησίμως αὐτοῖς ὁ τῶν ὅλων Κύριος καὶ ἐπ' αὐτοῦ βεβηκὼς ἐφαίνετο τοῦ στερεώματος, ἵν' εἰδεῖεν ὅτι πάντα ὑπὸ πόδας ἔχει, καὶ αὐτῶν ἐστι τῶν οὐρανῶν δεσπότης, ὡς δημιουργός. Συνίης οὖν ὅτι τύπον ὥσπερ τινὰ καὶ εἰκονισμὸν οὐρανοῦ τὸ Γράμμα ποιεῖται τὸ ἱερὸν, τὴν ὡς ἐν μετρίῳ φωτὶ κατωχριῶσαν λίθον; κυαναυγὴς γὰρ φύσει. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄριστα ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐρανοῦ δὴ οὖν σημεῖον ἡ σμάραγδος, γεγραμμένον ἔχουσα κατὰ γένος τὸν Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ τόπον λαχοῦσα τὴν ἐπωμίδα, δι' οὗ παρέσται νοεῖν, ὡς, οἵπερ ἂν εἶεν τὴν ἀπογραφὴν λαχόντες ἐν οὐρανῷ, οὗτοι πάντη τε καὶ πάντως ἐπαναπαύσονται τῷ Χριστῷ, μονονουχὶ καὶ ἐπ' ὤμων ἔχοντι, καὶ ὡς ἐν τάξει τέκνων ποιουμένῳ τοὺς ἀγαθούς. Τοιοῦτον δὲ καὶ ὁ θεῖος ἔφη Μωσῆς, φειδοῖ τῇ παρὰ Θεοῦ κατακαλλύνων τὸν Ἰσραήλ· «Ὡς ἀετὸς σκεπάσαι νοσσιὰν ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς νεοσσοῖς αὐτοῦ ἐπεπόθησε, διεὶς τὰς πτέρυγας αὐτοῦ ἐδέξατο αὐτοὺς, καὶ ἀνέλαβεν αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ τῶν μεταφρένων αὐτοῦ.» Ἀλλὰ δή που καὶ ὁ Δαβὶδ ἀναμελῳδεῖ ἁγίῳ παντὶ, καὶ ἐν βοηθείᾳ τοῦ Ὑψίστου κατῳκηκότι, «Ἐπὶ τῶν μεταφρένων αὐτοῦ ἐπισκιάσει σοι,» φησί. Μετάφρενά που καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι τὰ ὑπαυχένια μέρη, καὶ τὰ ὡς ἐν ὤμοις ὑποδηλῶν, καὶ οὐχὶ δὴ πάντως τὰ νῶτα. Ἐπ' ὤμων δὴ οὖν ἀρθήσονται, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ προφήτου φωνὴν, καὶ ἐπὶ βραχίονος ἀναληφθήσονται κατὰ τὸν ἀρχαῖον Ἐφραῒμ, οἱ τὴν ἄνω λαχόντες ἀπογραφὴν, ἣν εὐκλεᾶ τε καὶ ἀξιάγαστον καὶ τῶν θείων χαρισμάτων τὸ κάλλος ὑπερκειμένην αὐτὸς ἀπέφηνεν ὁ Σωτὴρ, τοῖς ἁγίοις μαθηταῖς ὡδίπη λέγων· «Μὴ χαίρετε ὅτι τὰ δαιμόνια ὑποτάσσεται ὑμῖν, χαίρετε δὲ μᾶλλον, ὅτι τὰ ὀνόματα ὑμῶν ἐγγέγραπται ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.» Μνημόσυνον δὲ τὴν ἔν γε τοῖς λίθοις ἀπογραφὴν ἔσεσθαί φησι τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ ἔναντι Κυρίου, μονονουχὶ καὶ ἐνατενίζοντος, ὡς ἐν Ἀαρών· εἰσδέχεται γὰρ ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ εἰς ἀνάμνησιν ἐν Χριστῷ, καὶ γεγόναμεν ἐν αὐτῷ γνώριμοί τε καὶ ἐποπτείας ἄξιοι, καὶ ὡς ἐν βίβλῳ Θεοῦ. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Κόσμημα δὲ τούτῳ καὶ ἕτερον προσεπάγεσθαι δεῖν ἐπιτάττει λέγων, «Καὶ ποιήσεις ἀσπιδίσκας ἐκ χρυσοῦ καθαροῦ καταμεμιγμένας, καὶ ποιήσεις δύο κροσσωτὰ ἐκ χρυσίου καθαροῦ καταμεμιγμένα ἐν ἄνθεσιν ἔργον πλοκῆς, καὶ ἐπιθήσεις τὰ κροσσωτὰ τὰ πεπλεγμένα ἐπὶ τὰς ἀσπιδίσκας καὶ τὰς παρωμίδας αὐτῶν ἐκ τῶν ἐμπροσθίων. Καὶ ποιήσεις λόγιον τῶν κρίσεων, ἔργον ὑφάντου κατὰ τὸν ῥυθμὸν τῆς ἐπωμίδος, ποιήσεις αὐτὸ ἐκ χρυσίου καὶ ὑακίνθου, καὶ πορφύρας καὶ κοκκίνου κεκλωσμένου, καὶ βύσσου κεκλωσμένης, ποιήσεις αὐτὸ τετράγωνον, ἔσται διπλοῦν σπιθαμῆς τὸ μῆκος καὶ σπιθαμῆς τὸ εὖρος, Καὶ καθυφανεῖς ἐν αὐτῷ ὕφασμα κατὰ τὸν
pass_a_gloss: CYR.: For since, having come to be in Egypt, those of Israel served (λελατρεύκασι) the creation (κτίσις) and called heaven god, usefully (χρησίμως) the Lord of all (τῶν ὅλων Κύριος) appeared having stepped (βεβηκώς) upon the firmament itself, so that they might know that he has all things under feet and is master (δεσπότης) of the heavens themselves, as craftsman (δημιουργός). Do you understand then that the holy Writing makes as a type (τύπος) and image-making (εἰκονισμός) of heaven the stone that is pale (κατωχριῶσαν) as in moderate light? For [it is] dark-blue-gleaming (κυαναυγής) by nature. PALL.: Excellently said. CYR.: A sign (σημεῖον) of heaven then is the emerald, having Israel written according to kin (κατὰ γένος), and having obtained (λαχοῦσα) as place the ephod; through which one may understand (νοεῖν) that those who have obtained the enrollment (ἀπογραφή) in heaven will in every way and wholly rest upon (ἐπαναπαύσονται) Christ, who all but (μονονουχί) has them on shoulders and makes (ποιουμένῳ) the good as in the rank (τάξις) of children. Such also the divine Moses said, adorning (κατακαλλύνων) Israel with the sparing care (φειδώ) from God: 'As an eagle would shelter (σκεπάσαι) its nest, and longed (ἐπεπόθησε) over its young, spreading its wings it received them and took them up on its back (μετάφρενα).' And David sings to every holy one who has settled in the help (βοήθεια) of the Most High: 'Upon his back he will overshadow (ἐπισκιάσει) you,' he says. Metaphrena, as I think, indicating the parts under the neck (ὑπαυχένια) and as at the shoulders, and not at all the back (νῶτα). On shoulders then they will be lifted (ἀρθήσονται), according to the voice of the prophet, and on the arm (βραχίων) taken up (ἀναληφθήσονται) according to the ancient Ephraim, those who obtained the enrollment above, which the Saviour himself showed to be glorious (εὐκλεᾶ), admirable (ἀξιάγαστον), and lying beyond (ὑπερκειμένην) the beauty of the divine gifts (χαρίσματα), saying thus somewhere to the holy disciples: 'Do not rejoice that the demons are subjected to you, but rejoice rather that your names are written in the heavens.' He says the enrollment on the stones will be a memorial for the sons of Israel before the Lord, who all but gazes intently (ἐνατενίζοντος), as in Aaron; for God and Father receives (εἰσδέχεται) us into remembrance (ἀνάμνησις) in Christ, and we have become in him known (γνώριμοι) and worthy of oversight (ἐποπτεία), and as in a book of God. PALL.: Rightly said. CYR.: He orders another ornament (κόσμημα) to be added to this, saying: 'And you will make little shields (ἀσπιδίσκαι) of pure gold, mixed (καταμεμιγμένας), and you will make two fringes (κροσσωτά) of pure gold mixed in flowers (ἄνθη), work of plaiting (πλοκή), and you will put the plaited fringes on the little shields and their shoulder-straps (παρωμίδες) from the front. And you will make the oracle of the judgments (λόγιον τῶν κρίσεων), weaver's work, according to the pattern (ῥυθμός) of the ephod; of gold, hyacinth, purple, spun scarlet, twisted linen; you will make it square (τετράγωνον); it will be double, a span (σπιθαμή) the length and a span the breadth. And you will weave into it a weaving according to the [continues: stone, four-rowed].'
pass_b_english: Cyril: For since the Israelites, while they lived in Egypt, had served the creation (Romans 1:25) and called heaven a god, the Lord of all appeared to them, for their good, standing upon the firmament itself, so that they might know that he has all things under his feet and is master of the heavens themselves, as their Creator. Do you see, then, that holy Scripture makes the stone, with its pallor as of a moderate light, a kind of type and image of heaven? For by nature it gleams dark blue.

Cyril: The emerald, then, is a sign of heaven. It has Israel written on it, family by family, and it has been given the ephod as its place. From this we may understand that those who have been granted enrollment in heaven will surely, and in every way, rest upon Christ, who all but carries them on his shoulders and counts the good in the rank of children. The divine Moses said something like this when he adorned Israel with the tender care that comes from God: ‘As an eagle would shelter its nest, and yearned over its young, spreading its wings it received them, and took them up on its back’ (Deuteronomy 32:11). David too sings to every holy one who has made his dwelling in the help of the Most High (Psalm 91:1): ‘He will overshadow you upon his back,’ he says (Psalm 91:4). By ‘back’ I take him to mean the parts just below the neck, the region, as it were, of the shoulders, and not the back as a whole. So, in the words of the prophet, they will be lifted up on shoulders (Isaiah 60:4; Isaiah 66:12), and, as with Ephraim of old, they will be taken up on the arm (Hosea 11:3): those who have been granted the enrollment above. The Savior himself declared that enrollment glorious and admirable, surpassing even the beauty of the divine gifts, when he said somewhere to the holy disciples: ‘Do not rejoice that the demons are subject to you, but rejoice rather that your names are written in heaven’ (Luke 10:20). And he says that the enrollment on the stones will be a remembrance for the sons of Israel before the Lord (Exodus 28:12), who all but fixes his gaze on them, as they are in Aaron. For God the Father receives us into remembrance in Christ, and in him we have become known to God and worthy of his watchful care, as though written in God’s book.

Cyril: He commands that yet another ornament be added to it, saying: ‘And you shall make little shields of pure gold, of mingled work, and you shall make two fringes of pure gold, mingled with flowers, a plaited work; and you shall put the plaited fringes on the little shields and on their shoulder straps at the front. And you shall make the oracle of judgments, the work of a weaver, after the design of the ephod; you shall make it of gold and blue and purple and twisted scarlet and twisted fine linen.
